findings.title: Table widget feature flag renders an empty table
findings.body: The new `use-table-widget-visualization` branch passes hard-coded empty `columns` and `tableData` (`data: []`, empty `meta.fields`/`units`) instead of the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, and `fields`. When the feature flag is enabled, every dashboard table widget will render with no rows or columns, so the feature is non-functional and existing dashboards appear empty. The branch must forward the actual table results or fall back to the existing table until it does.

findings.title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore records
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` zips `error_ids` with `events.values()` from `nodestore.backend.get_multi`. If any event is missing, `get_multi` omits it from the returned dict, so `.values()` shifts and later error IDs can be associated with the wrong event data. That produces incorrect error titles/messages in generated summaries. Iterate over the node IDs and use `events.get(node_id)` so missing entries remain aligned with their `error_ids`.

findings.title: New PR comment helpers are called on the wrong class
findings.body: `get_comment_body` calls `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(issue)`. Those helpers were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` is a `PRCommentWorkflow` that holds an integration rather than inheriting from it. Building a suspect PR comment will therefore raise `AttributeError`; the GitLab workflow has the same issue. The helpers should live on `PRCommentWorkflow` or be called through `self.integration`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` should not reference `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` unless that method exists there.

findings.title: 60-second deadline can leave an auth identity batch unprocessed
findings.body: `check_auth` marks `last_synced` for every selected identity before scheduling `check_auth_identities`, and that task processes up to 100 identities sequentially and only reschedules at the end. A 60-second processing deadline can kill the task before it finishes or reaches the reschedule, leaving the remaining identities unprocessed until the next ~24-hour cycle. Increase/remove the deadline, or update/reschedule identities incrementally so a timeout does not silently skip work.

findings.title: Custom renderer return value is checked by truthiness
findings.body: `if (cell)` treats valid custom renderer results like `0` or the empty string as “no custom renderer” and falls back to the default renderer. Any table cell intentionally rendered as a falsy value will be rendered incorrectly. Check `cell !== undefined` (and similarly for the head renderer at line 32).

findings.title: Zero values bypass age/timestamp mutual exclusion
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test `self.initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. Since `0` is a valid value for both `age` and `timestamp`, a report containing both fields can pass validation when the conflicting value is `0`. Use an explicit `is not None` check so zero does not bypass the mutual-exclusion rule.
